results.title: What Is the Seniority System in Congress?
results.content: The Seniority System: How Power is Amassed in Congress. The Effects of the Seniority System on How Congress Works. * The seniority system gives long-serving Congress members perks like choosing their offices and committee roles. The seniority system has been the target of numerous reform initiatives over the years, all of which have failed to prevent the most senior members of Congress from amassing tremendous power. Members with a longer term of service on a committee are also assumed to be senior, and therefore they have more power within the committee. The seniority system enhances the power of the committee chairs (limited to six years since 1995) because they are no longer beholden to the interests of party leaders. Sincethere are no term limits for members of Congress, this means members with seniority can, and do, amass great amounts of power and influence.
